findings.title: Schematic sheet notes still describe superseded parts: U4 as LSM6DSV320X (+/-32..320 g, DS14623) and a camera-regulator 'U8' USB self-test

evidence.file: m3_design/assembly_review/sensors.kicad_sch (text at line 1853); m3_design/assembly_review/diagnostics.kicad_sch (CAM_5V_SENSE note); m3_design/assembly_review/m3.kicad_sch ('battery alone feeds camera')
evidence.measured: sensors note reads 'U4 = ST LSM6DSV320X (R4): +/-16 g low-g + +/-32..320 g high-g accel ... Pins 10/11 open per DS14623 table 2'; the other U4 notes cite DS14623 table 25. Board U4 = ISM6HG256X, LCSC C51931514, MPN ISM6HG256XTR (pcbnew), symbol Value ISM6HG256X. DS15034 Rev 1 p1: high-g +/-32/64/128/256 g (no 320 g); D-R19-11 / binding note restrict firmware to high-g codes 001 / 010 because code 100 is +/-256 g on the ISM and +/-320 g on the LSM. The pins 10/11 obligation itself holds for the ISM: DS15034 Table 25 (p52) has the same internal pull-ups and OIS_PU_DIS in PIN_CTRL (02h). diagnostics note: 'Lets the USB self-test verify the camera regulator (U8)': no U8 among the 215 footprints (camera buck is U400, switch U402), and on USB-only power PORT_5V3 is off (camera rail from protected battery only).

findings.impact: The schematic is the declared single source of truth (AGENTS section 3). A firmware author reading sheet 03 gets the alternate part's 320 g range and datasheet; on the fitted part the matching code is reserved / different (D-R19-11). The self-test note names a part that does not exist and a test that cannot run on USB power.
findings.concrete_fix: In r10_sch.py: replace the U4 note with 'U4 = ST ISM6HG256X (D-R19-11; LSM6DSV320X consigned alternate, same land): +/-16 g low-g, +/-32..256 g high-g (use FS codes 001/010 only), +/-4000 dps; pins 10/11 open, internal pull-ups, keep OIS_PU_DIS = 0 (DS15034 Table 25)', cite DS15034 in the two other U4 notes; change the CAM_5V_SENSE note to 'verifies U400/U402 on battery power'. Text only; schematic notes are not in the PCB hash.

findings.title: The single-switch arming chain (BAT_SW_SOURCE, BAT_SW_RETURN, BAT_ENABLE) is not in route_check's pyro/arming critical class, and no record says why

evidence.measured: The R10 pyro class regex covers PYRO1_*, ARM1_*, ACT_GATE/DRV/EN, ACT_EN_MCU only; route.json gives BAT_ENABLE cls 'other'. Instances that would be critical hygiene: tiny_jog BAT_ENABLE B.Cu (21.0, 68.6) -> (21.3, 68.9), mid 0.424 mm, offset 0.3 mm (counted as a noncritical leftover); short_layer_hop B.Cu (19.675, 66.6) 2.973 mm and extra_bends F.Cu (21.3, 68.9) -> (17.1, 82.8) (information). BAT_ENABLE has three vias, nearest GND via 1.423 / 1.866 / 2.902 mm, total track 27.93 mm (pcbnew). F8 / AGENTS section 2.1 make J400 the pad arming device; AGENTS section 3 and REQUIREMENTS M2 list 'pyro and arming' nets as critical.
evidence.physics: BAT_ENABLE is a 227 kohm / 220 nF node (tau 50 ms), so the 1.5 mm GND partner-via rule has no return-path root there and would be AUD-2-exempt like ACT_GATE (which also has vias 1.707 / 5.916 mm from GND). The gap is the class and the critical hygiene, not return path.

findings.impact: Under the R10 single-switch scope the arming device's nets get only noncritical hygiene, while the owner's clean-routing criterion (M2) gates arming nets. The classification is a silent scope choice rather than a recorded decision; S-6 (round 19 gate) already treats the chain as safety-relevant.
findings.concrete_fix: Either add ^(BAT_ENABLE|BAT_SW_SOURCE|BAT_SW_RETURN)$ to the R10 pyro class and to critical_reference.R10_SLOW_RETURN_NETS (AUD-2 partner-via exemption), then remove the (21.0, 68.6) jog at the next board change (it touches the D-R20-01 EN cell) or list it in the R10 deviation table; or record in M2 / R10_VALIDATION why the switch-enable chain is not an arming net. Gate / records only now.

findings.title: Flight envelope: the flight-2 altitude and duration (3.4-3.6 km, 460-525 s) do not fit the Mach 1.9 design point, and flight 1 (K850DM) still has no envelope

evidence.file: docs/REQUIREMENTS.md lines 28-46 (flight table), line 89 (Temperature: 'flight 2 lasts up to 525 s'); ../../docs/VEHICLE.md (Mass and CG: K850DM budget not done)
evidence.measured: Mach 1.9 is about 650 m/s near the ground. A drag-free coast gives v^2 / 2g = 650^2 / 19.6 = 21.5 km; a 54 mm minimum-diameter airframe loses much of that to drag, but the apogee is unlikely to be as low as 3.4-3.6 km (Inference; no trajectory run here). The table itself says 'update for the current vehicle and Mach 1.9 design point'; flight 1 says 'Recalculate for K850DM'.
evidence.board_effect: None found (Inference): at a 6 km / 800 s flight the F5 log is about 500 Hz x 40 B x ~70 s + 50 Hz x 40 B x ~800 s = 3 MB against 16 MB QSPI; F3's 10 km barometer requirement then has a physical root rather than being spare margin; MCU thermal (Temperature row) is a steady-state argument at 200 MHz.

findings.impact: Requirements that consume duration (Temperature row 525 s, pad-energy Q_flight, F5 log windows) and the F2 37 g peak are rooted in a pre-Mach-1.9 estimate. The board appears to cover the corrected case, but no record shows it.
findings.concrete_fix: Mark the 3.4-3.6 km / 460-525 s / 28-37 g row as a pre-Mach-1.9 estimate and replace it from the OpenRocket model of the current vehicle (both motors) before order acceptance; re-check F5 window, pad-energy Q_flight and the 525 s Temperature figure against it. Records only.
